Synopsis:
    Following an Iran war, oil vessel transit costs through the Strait of Hormuz have surged dramatically. Cargo insurance now runs up to 5-6% of cargo value (~$10M), and additional war risk premiums have jumped from zero to up to 10% of cargo value, pushing total transit costs into the $10-20M range. Some market participants are self-insuring. NOCs are increasingly taking back control of their own shipping to manage costs and flexibility. Shipowner willingness to operate in the area is constrained by safety concerns. Cargo flows are being rerouted onto longer, more complex routes, reshaping freight economics and vessel availability globally.

Q02. Is the content confirming already known information or reporting very new/uncertain risks?
Risk score: 75 — A kinetic Iran war scenario with sustained Hormuz disruption is a major escalation beyond pre-existing risk assumptions. The specific cost figures and structural shifts (NOC self-shipping, near-total market withdrawal of private shipowners) represent genuinely new and uncertain market conditions, though Hormuz risk as a concept is well understood.
